US Army to detonate unstable lead-based explosives in Iowa
November 25, 2026
The Army says a controlled blast is the safest way to deal with explosive chemicals that began crystallising in storage, but residents say changing guidance has left them confused about where the lead dust will go.
The United States Army plans to detonate about 5 tons of aging lead azide at an Iowa ammunition plant on Wednesday, saying the explosive chemical has become too unstable to store.
The controlled blast is set for 9 am local time (1500 GMT) at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, and will destroy the country's entire stockpile of the chemical.
The US army has said residents of a small town and other nearby areas should leave "out of an abundance of caution."
"We don’t believe that the public should be in a panic," said acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle. "Our goal is to keep as much of it as we can here on our Iowa Army Ammunition plant to prevent it from traveling."
What do we know?
The material was moved to Iowa for storage from bases around the country in 2009.
But a March inspection found that it had partly crystallized, which makes it sensitive to friction and cold and could set off a spontaneous explosion.
"Inaction is no longer an option," said Major General Eric Shirley, who leads the operation.
Rob Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, told reporters: "It's not a matter of if, it's a matter of when, and that would not be a great place for us to be in."
Is it safe to detonate the chemical?
To limit toxic lead dust, the Army has built barriers around the bunkers holding the material and will use foam and water to trap particles.
Reuters reported that Army projections show dust could settle up to 40 miles (64 km) southwest, reaching northern Missouri.
Officials expect the wind to carry the plume away from Burlington, a city of nearly 25,000 people.
While residents within 5 miles (8 km) were encouraged to evacuate, the Federal Emergency Management Agency has also advised people 5 to 20 miles away to stay indoors with windows closed.
How have people reacted?
The date of the detonation changed three times after public backlash. A federal appeals court cleared the plan on Monday after environmental groups sued.
Farmer Jill Holler, who organised a protest, told Reuters: "I'm not opposed if this is the only safe option."
"What I'm saying is that it's been so mishandled that people are confused and don't trust anything they're saying," she added.
digest_he:
צבא ארצות הברית הודיע על כוונה לבצע פיצוץ מבוקר של כחמישה טון חומרי נפץ ישנים מסוג עופרת אזיד במפעל תחמושת באיווה. הצעד מגיע לאחר שבדיקה שנערכה במרץ העלתה כי החומרים החלו להתגבש, דבר שהופך אותם לרגישים מאוד ומעלה חשש מפני פיצוץ ספונטני בלתי צפוי.

המבצע המתוכנן נועד לחסל את כלל מאגרי החומר הללו במדינה בדרך הבטוחה ביותר האפשרית, למרות החששות הכבדים בקרב תושבי האזור מפני פיזור אבק עופרת רעיל. הצבא הקים מחסומים מיוחדים וישתמש בקצף ומים כדי ללכוד את החלקיקים, אך קיימות תחזיות לפיהן האבק עלול לנדוד למרחקים של עשרות קילומטרים.

הרשויות המקומיות והפדרליות המליצו לתושבים בקרבת מקום להתפנות או לשהות בבתים סגורים כצעד מונע. למרות שעתירות משפטיות של ארגוני איכות סביבה נדחו, תושבים מקומיים הביעו תסכול רב וטענו כי חוסר העקביות בהנחיות הרשמיות פגע באמון הציבור בתהליך.
